items.why_relevant: Training entry point. Calls trainer.step per batch (line 110). trainer.step is filter_jit'd. No sparse application in training loop yet; SparseMaskManager.step() must be invoked outside jit if used.

items.excerpt: def apply_mask(self, weights: Array, mask: Array) -> Array | BCOO
items.why_relevant: Core sparse application. Returns either dense (weights * mask) or BCOO with fixed nse=nse_budget. Line 31-32 comment: 'Eager Python-side only — NOT safe under filter_jit/jax.jit. n_true branches on a traced Array under jit → TracerBoolConversionError.' Must be called outside jit.

items.excerpt: def make_mask(self, weights: Array, step: int) -> Array
items.why_relevant: Mask generation. Uses argsort to select EXACTLY nse_budget True values (no threshold ties). Returns jnp.bool_ array with shape=weights.shape.

Python-side mutable mask tracker. line 28-51: step() method updates masks (if schedule says so) and applies them via tree_map_with_path. Line 33: should_update = not initialized OR policy.should_update(step). Line 51: applies via tree_map_with_path (Python-side tree traversal).

items.excerpt: def step(self, params: PyTree, step: int, path_filter: Callable = ...) -> PyTree
items.why_relevant: Applies current masks to params via tree_map_with_path. Returns params with sparse structure applied (BCOO or dense). Must be called OUTSIDE jit/filter_jit because apply_mask branches on traced values.

items.why_relevant: Unified dispatch over 4 AxisStrategy variants (Vmap, SafeMap, Scan, DedupGather). Lines 40-61 exhaustively match each variant. No mention of static shapes or padding for retrace avoidance yet.

Incomplete. Meant to bucket data by boundaries with different batch_sizes per bucket. Constructor takes boundaries, batch_sizes, fn, xs. Current implementation is a stub (line 132 'yield from []'). NOT functional yet.
Sealed union for tiling strategies. No retrace-safety or bucket-padding semantics yet. SafeMap has batch_size field (threshold + chunk size).

BCOO is the sparse format returned by apply_mask when nse < nse_budget. Fixed-nse padding (line 45: size=nse_budget, fill_value=0) ensures deterministic indices; validity_mask (line 46) zeros unused slots.

items.excerpt: Verifies that apply_mask returns BCOO with nse == nse_budget (fixed)
items.why_relevant: Tests confirm BCOO has fixed nse=nse_budget (line 39: assert result.nse == 4). This is the key to avoiding retrace: shape of indices and data arrays are static.

items.excerpt: Tests that padding slots (0,0) are zeroed via validity_mask
items.why_relevant: Confirms that fixed-nse BCOO correctly handles fewer True values than nse_budget: padded slots are zeroed, not aliased to weight[0,0].
Existing pattern: Engine.eval wraps model in eqx.nn.inference_mode before iteration (line 169). This disables dropout/stochastic layers. No sparse-aware variant yet.

items.excerpt: n_true branches on a traced Array under jit → TracerBoolConversionError
items.why_relevant: CRITICAL: apply_mask uses n_true = jnp.sum(mask) to decide fallback path (line 34-42). This is NOT safe under jit because n_true is a traced scalar. Branching on it causes retrace. Fixed-nse BCOO avoids retrace by using static size=nse_budget in argwhere (line 45).

Static, non-traced constant. Used as size parameter in argwhere (fixed-size indices). Key to avoiding retrace: when apply_mask always produces BCOO with nse=nse_budget, JAX doesn't need to retrace when inputs have static shapes.

items.excerpt: @eqx.filter_jit def step(self, state: ResumableState, batch: Any) -> tuple[ResumableState, dict]
items.why_relevant: Training step is filter_jit'd. Calls loss_fn(model(batch['inputs']), ...) inside jit. If SparseMaskManager.step were called inside jit, it would fail (apply_mask not jit-safe). Must be applied before filter_jit.
Safety variant also filter_jit'd. Same constraint: sparse mask application must occur outside jit.
